analyst_view.overall: Early view: Atalanta (16th, four points) under Maurizio Sarri are short of players: Gianluca Gaetano, Raoul Bellanova, Thomas Kristensen, Isak Hien, Giacomo Raspadori and Odilon Kossounou were all missing at Monza on 8 November. The 1-0 win there, through Nikola Krstovic, ended a run of six games without a win since 15 October, including a 3-0 home defeat by Parma and a 1-1 draw with Kairat. Borac (21st, three points) beat KuPS 2-0 at home and lost narrowly at Panathinaikos.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, 2.0 for Atalanta. Atalanta's recent games swing widely (a 4-4 with Frosinone and a 2-2 at Fiorentina, then 1-1 and 1-0), so their defence is not reliable, but their injury-hit attack has also scored only twice in the last two games. Those cancel out, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, 6.0 for Atalanta. Sarri's teams keep the ball and Borac should defend deep at home for long spells, which the split already reflects.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. Atalanta picked up two bookings at Monza (Éderson and Charles De Ketelaere) in a scrappy game; there is no referee yet and nothing in Borac's games points away from the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots, 18.9 for Atalanta. I lean lower: with Raspadori, Gaetano and several defenders out, Atalanta's attack has been blunt lately, and Monza had the better of the first half against them. I expect a high count, but below the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. For the same reasons as the shots, a thin, out-of-form Atalanta side, I lean slightly lower.
